text:
jules: quick heads-up — Galatea13b int4 canary hitting intermittent OOMs under light concurrency (2-3 reqs). Memory trace shows KV churn + short-lived spikes after generation starts.

mike: repro steps? logs?

jules: posting snippets. happens on V100 pool and on a1-dedicated nodes. minimal prompt, then after ~max_new_tokens/2 we see a sudden +1.2GB allocation and then OOM.

jules: ```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] alloc(1200MB) at attention_kv.cu:142
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] evict: 0 -> 32 slots reclaimed
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] alloc(1280MB) at kv_cache.cu:88
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] OOM: failed to allocate 1280MB
```

eva: looks like prefetch + aggressive max_new_tokens default is causing working set blowup. our int4 kernels keep temporary activations in GPU memory longer.

sara: what are current defaults for Galatea?

mike: current defaults: `max_new_tokens=256`, `microbatch_size=2`, `prefetch_kv=96`, `soft_reserve=5%` (hosted profile).

jules: proposal: dial back defaults for this canary and run targeted bisect. suggestions: drop max_new_tokens to 128, microbatch_size -> 1, prefetch_kv -> 32, soft_reserve -> 10%. also enable KV adaptive eviction heuristic (ttl-based). quick config snippet:```
model_config:
  max_new_tokens: 128
  microbatch_size: 1
  prefetch_kv: 32
  kv_eviction_policy: adaptive_ttl
  soft_reserve_pct: 10
```

ops-bot: deploy job #4523 started: canary/galatea13b/int4-quant -> 3 nodes

eva: run quality quickcheck before/after. last eval vs fp16 showed -0.8% on long-form generative pass (coherence metrics). need to confirm whether reduced tokens or microbatch changes affect quality.

mike: ran small eval locally — difference seems concentrated in commonsense prompts (layernorm rounding). possible mitigation: hybrid activations (fp16 for layernorm + int4 elsewhere) or per-layer fallback for top 3 decoder layers.

jules: hybrid fallback sounds safest for now. tradeoffs: ~6% token cost increase but eliminates OOM and recovers ~0.6% quality.

sara: action items: 1) @mike implement config and run canary (est 20m). 2) @eva run eval harness with 1k prompts and perf+quality diffs. 3) @jules monitor KV churn metrics and GPU mem timeline. if canary stabilizes, we push adjusted defaults to onboard profile.

mike: doing step 1 now. canary command: `run_canary --model galatea13b --variant int4-hybrid-fallback --nodes 3 --config experiments/galatea/int4-hybrid-01.yaml`

jules: note for postmortem if this recurs — capture `KV_CHURN_RATE`, `prefetch_kv`, `alloc_highwater` and `evict_count` every 10s for 5m window. also keep the original failing seed/prompts.

eva: small wrinkle — metrics show latency tail increases when soft_reserve is high because we throttle earlier. fine for canary but may need a middle ground for prod. propose soft_reserve 8% for dedicated tier.

ops-bot: deploy job #4523 succeeded on node-03, node-04, node-05. health checks green.

mike: canary run completed (30m). no OOMs in 3-node run at 50 RPS synthetic load. memory highwater ~5.8GB (was 7.4GB before).

eva: eval results in — quality delta vs fp16: -0.15% overall, long-form gap reduced to -0.2%. good compromise.

jules: recommend landing these defaults for Galatea13b int4 profile: `max_new_tokens=128`, `microbatch_size=1`, `prefetch_kv=32`, `soft_reserve=8%`, `int4-hybrid-layer-fallback=top3`. i can draft rollout PR.

sara: please add smoke playbook to the PR and include quick rollback steps: `pin model to fp16`, `reduce concurrency`, `revert profile`.

mike: PR opened #4821 with config, smoke tests, and bench .yaml. linking bench: https://internal/redwood/bench/galatea/int4-hybrid-01

jules: thanks all. closing loop — leaving thread open for another 24h to watch additional canary traffic. :thumbsup:
